text: Rust allows only one mutable reference to a value at a time so the compiler can treat that reference as the only live path to the data and reject conflicting access before the program runs. That rule prevents data races, where one part of the program writes memory while another reads or writes it without synchronization.
thought:
This is a conceptual question about Rust's borrow checker.

Rust enforces a single mutable reference to any value at once. This prevents data races.

It also prevents memory unsafety from mutable aliasing. Concurrent data races and iterator invalidation are the main risks.
